posts.title: Watch parallel coding agents locally
posts.promise: Spot stuck, drifting or conflicting coding agents and leave the nudge to a person.
posts.whatItIs: Tracon is a local monitor for parallel Claude Code agents. Its README says it reads session transcripts and worktree state, then shows agents that are blocked, idle, looping, drifting or editing the same files. A small student version could watch one project session and display a short status list; it would not need to control the agents.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: developers or small teams coordinating several coding agents might pay for better visibility. The sources establish no customers or willingness to pay.
loop: Read the local coding-agent session and worktree state.
Refresh a list of active agents and their current status.
Flag permission waits, repeated failures, drift or overlapping file edits.
Show a person the relevant session details and history.
Let the person decide whether to send a suggested nudge to the lead agent.
The person reviews agent output and decides what to merge.
posts.evidence: The public README describes a terminal and browser monitor, local transcript and worktree inspection, optional checks against agent briefs, and a demo mode with a made-up run. It says the tool sends a note only after the user presses n. The README does not establish customer use or commercial demand.
posts.uncertainty: This is a real documented project, but its demonstration is explicitly made up. A student version could monitor one local session; it would need coding-agent transcript access and platform testing. It reports signals rather than guaranteeing correct diagnoses, and a person must investigate, nudge and review code.
first24Hours: Install the documented demo in a disposable project and note each status it displays.
Write down a narrow one-session status list and identify which signals can be read safely.
Sketch a read-only dashboard and list failure cases that must be escalated to a person.

feasibility.reason: A limited local monitor can focus on one session, while transcript parsing and environment setup add work.

autonomy.reason: Repeated local monitoring flags stuck or drifting agents; a person investigates and chooses whether to nudge.

steps.message: Assessed the 12 selected enrichment leads. Tracon is proposed after its README supplied fresh primary evidence beyond the earlier title-only refusal; its five provisional ratings average 6.0, the frozen threshold. Eleven others are excluded for insufficient evidence, lack of a bounded beginner loop, or excessive scope.
